about: Absorbers, strippers and columns with nonvolatile components (proposal 0015, Part II, step 7; milestone M3; proposal 0009, step 5). Conventions as validation/data/columns/README.md: mol/s, K, kPa, J/mol, W; stages numbered from the top; no pressure drop. Without a condenser stage 1 is an equilibrium stage whose vapour leaves the column (the top gas); without a reboiler stage N is one whose liquid leaves it (the bottom liquid). A feed is given by its temperature and phase (liquid or vapour, its molar enthalpy h_L or h_V there), or as a saturated vapour (at its dew point at the column's pressure). duties_W: heat added to a stage (negative: removed). Reference: validation/python/reference_mesh_absorber.py, fixture validation/fixtures/columns_absorber.json, test test/columns-absorber.test.js.

cases.title: Model absorber, 6 stages, a solute of constant K = 0.8 in constant flows: the Kremser equation
cases.purpose: An exact answer. The model system of the M2a cases (h_L = 0, h_V = the latent heat for every component) keeps L and V constant on every stage; the solute A has a constant K, so its fraction not absorbed is the Kremser equation's, (A_f - 1) / (A_f^(N+1) - 1) with A_f = L / (K V), exactly. The carrier gas G and the solvent S carry the temperature (K = alpha p(T) / P, ln(p/kPa) = 16 - 4000/T, alphas 50 and 1).
cases.method_choice: a model system (no real mixture: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md does not apply)

cases.title: Ammonia from air into water, 8 stages, adiabatic: The ChemSep Book's absorber problem with its K-value and enthalpy polynomials
cases.purpose: A published problem with strong heat effects (the absorption heats the liquid, which raises ammonia's K: a temperature bulge inside the column). The gas, the K-values and the enthalpies are the book's; the water flow (400 mol/s at 20 degC) and the 8 stages are this case's choice (the book asks for the design and prints no solution), so the check is against the independent reference, not against published numbers.

source.citation: H. A. Kooijman and R. Taylor, The ChemSep Book, 2nd edition (2006), section 1.6.7 'Absorber Design', Table 1.4 (p. 42-43); the problem is attributed there to Seader and Henley, Separation Process Principles (1998), section 11.7
source.access: free to download from chemsep.org; the book is placed in the public domain by its authors
source.printed: gas 80 mol/s, ammonia 0.416, air 0.584, 20 degC, 1 atm; K_i = alpha_i + beta_i T (T in K); H_V,i = A_i + B_i T; H_L,i = a_i + b_i T, in J/kmol: ammonia alpha -32.285, beta 0.1137, A 3.57e7, B 3.52e4, a 0, b 7.5e4; water -1.231833, 0.00427325, 4.3486e7, 3.35e4, 0, 7.5e4; air -191835, 900, 0, 2.92e4, 0, 7.5e4

cases.method_choice: the book's correlations (the problem says the appropriate model, Henry's law, is not available, and gives these polynomials instead); CHEPTA's own methods for ammonia + water + air are not used

cases.title: H2 with 100 kW removed from stage 6, where the temperature bulge is (an intercooler)
cases.purpose: A stage duty: the energy balance of stage 6 holds with Q = -100 kW, and the column's overall balance closes with it.

cases.title: Methanol stripped from water by live steam, 10 stages, NRTL
cases.purpose: A stripper without a reboiler: a liquid at the top, saturated steam at the bottom; methanol leaves with the top vapour.
cases.method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rule 3: polar, no electrolytes, 1 atm, fitted pairs: NRTL with an ideal-gas vapour (CHEPTA's default methanol + water set)

cases.title: The H4 liquid stripped in a reboiled stripper, 10 stages, boil-up ratio 0.25, NRTL
cases.purpose: A stripper with a reboiler and no condenser: one specification, at the bottom.

cases.title: Light hydrocarbons absorbed in n-decane at 2000 kPa, 6 stages, Peng-Robinson
cases.purpose: A gas absorber with real components: methane passes, propane and n-butane are absorbed, some n-decane leaves with the gas.
cases.method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 1 and 2: nonpolar hydrocarbons and light gases: Peng-Robinson (the databank's k_ij)

cases.title: Methanol from water and lactic acid (nonvolatile), 10 stages, total condenser, ideal solution
cases.purpose: A distillation with a nonvolatile component: lactic acid stays in the liquid and leaves entirely with the bottoms.
cases.method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rule 3 would choose an activity model; CHEPTA has no NRTL or UNIQUAC pair with lactic acid, so the independent reference uses the ideal solution (Raoult's law, ideal-gas vapour), which test/nonvolatile.test.js also uses; the engine is also run with Modified UNIFAC 2.0 (predicted tier), without a reference

cases.title: Water and lactic acid (nonvolatile) in a reboiled stripper boiled nearly dry: bottoms 1.05 mol/s for 1 mol/s of lactic acid
cases.purpose: A stage that would dry out: the bottom liquid is about 95 % lactic acid, its volatile part far below 1 % of the column's vapour: DRY_STAGE on the reboiler. A bottoms flow at or below the lactic acid's (1 mol/s) is refused (BAD_INPUT).
cases.method_choice: as H7; without methanol, whose liquid records stop below the bottom stage's temperature (about 490 K)

cases.title: Carbon dioxide and nitrogen washed with water at 1000 kPa, 8 stages: CO2 and N2 dissolve by Henry's law (IAPWS G7-04)
cases.purpose: An absorber with Henry components (proposal 0017; the maintainer, 2026-11-04): in an activity model with water the gases dissolve by f = H x (unsymmetric convention, activity coefficient 1 at infinite dilution), water by Raoult's law; the liquid enthalpy of a dissolved gas is its ideal-gas enthalpy minus R T^2 d ln H / dT.
cases.method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md step 2 and proposal 0017: an activity model with Henry's law for gases dissolving in water (NRTL is named; with water the only solvent its parameters are not used)
